source.title: Residual Pathway Priors for Soft Equivariance Constraints
source.authors: Marc Finzi; Gregory W. Benton; A. Wilson

record.tranche_reason: The study compares convolutional and fully connected models on CIFAR-10, reporting test classification error; it uses its own RPP method and does not reproduce the cited studies' methods.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports test classification error for MLP, RPP, and Conv on CIFAR-10. The cited 14% result for locally connected MLPs is prior work and is not extracted as a result.
record.test_reason: Table 1 directly tests V3 by comparing held-out CIFAR-10 classification error for convolutional and fully connected models trained with Adam. The study is not an original source for V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the Table 1 conclusion. The broader conclusion is that RPPs soften architectural constraints while preserving flexibility: they approach constrained-model performance under exact symmetries, MLP performance under misspecified symmetries, and can outperform both under approximate symmetries. The paper also reports reinforcement-learning instability on Humanoid.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates RPP models and convolutional models on CIFAR-10; it does not reproduce the cited comparison methods. The RPP model is an MLP with larger prior variance in the convolutional subspace.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported result varies by architecture: MLP, RPP, and Conv have different test errors on CIFAR-10.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 also compares convolutional models, MLPs, and RPPs on four UCI regression tasks whose inputs are reshaped into arrays.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The usefulness of convolutional structure depends on whether it matches the data; image-classification advantages need not transfer to reshaped tabular regression.

record.problems: For the claim's architecture comparison, the study reports only CIFAR-10 results. Its RPP model is an MLP with a convolutional-subspace prior, so it is not a plain fully connected comparator.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Other image datasets; separating locality from weight sharing; learning sparse local connections; initializing a fully connected model from a trained convolutional model.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and effects of tuning or optimizer switching.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout comparisons and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The CIFAR-10 results do not establish that locality alone explains the advantage. The 14% locally connected MLP result is cited prior work, not this study's result. No optimizer, dropout, batch-size, or sharpness comparison follows merely from the training recipe.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
MNIST, CIFAR-100, and SVHN; learning sparse local connections in fully connected networks; and initializing a fully connected network from a trained convolutional network.
Adaptive optimizer comparisons and their tuning or regularization conditions.
Large-batch training and its recipe-dependent effects.
Dropout effects and its interaction with data augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: MLP
rows.size_stated: 9 convolutional layers and 1 fully connected layer in the equivalent architecture; channel sizes 16, 16, 16, 32, 32, 32, 32, 32, 32
rows.operation_detail: Trained the equivalent MLP architecture on CIFAR-10 for 200 epochs using Adam and a cosine learning-rate schedule.
rows.note: The text says the model is still an MLP and has larger prior variance in the convolutional subspace.
rows.check: The value is correct: 37.61 ± 0.56% test error, versus Conv's 12.03 ± 0.46%. The note incorrectly attributes the convolutional-subspace prior to the ordinary MLP; that description applies to RPP. The listed convolutional layers describe the corresponding CNN architecture, not literal convolutional layers in the MLP.

rows.subject: RPP
rows.size_stated: 9 convolutional layers and 1 fully connected layer in the equivalent architecture; channel sizes 16, 16, 16, 32, 32, 32, 32, 32, 32
rows.operation_detail: Trained the RPP model on CIFAR-10 for 200 epochs using Adam and a cosine learning-rate schedule.
rows.note: The authors describe this model as an MLP with larger prior variance in the convolutional subspace.
rows.check: The value is correct: 12.62 ± 0.34% test error. This is an expressive MLP with an explicit convolutional-subspace prior, not an ordinary fully connected baseline. Relative to Conv's 12.03 ± 0.46%, the convolutional advantage is much smaller than against the ordinary MLP. It does not isolate learned sparse local connectivity.

relationships.display_finding: CNN test error was 12.03 ± 0.46%, versus 37.61 ± 0.56% for the ordinary MLP without the convolutional-subspace prior.
